script: The first pulsar was discovered in 1967 by astronomer Jocelyn Bell Burnell. Its radio signal pulsed so regularly that it was nicknamed LGM-1. That stood for Little Green Men, a joke about aliens. It turned out to be a spinning neutron star sweeping beams across space. Some pulsars keep time almost as accurately as atomic clocks.
